sampling_method: Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in reading order (location order below, row-major within a table/paragraph), giving a population of 1..262. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(population, 15) drew {1, 3, 23, 25, 28, 49, 57, 139, 157, 166, 182, 197, 214, 216, 244}; each label below records its draw as frame_index.
labelling_notes: Two judgement calls materially affect the frame count and are recorded here for audit. (1) Table 3 (Zero-shot Evaluations) baseline rows (Pythia, RWKV, Hybrid H3, GPT-Neo, OPT, GPT-J) are read as citation baselines, not own reimplementations: the paper names them by citation, and each baseline's tested sizes match that model family's own public release ladder (e.g. RWKV-1.5B/3B/7.4B) rather than Mamba's matched-FLOPs scaling ladder, unlike the cases below where the paper states the authors themselves trained or measured the baseline. Only Table 3's 5 Mamba rows (45 of up to 216 candidate cells) enter the frame. (2) Conversely, several baseline-named rows elsewhere ARE counted as own results because the paper states or clearly implies the authors trained/measured that exact configuration themselves for a controlled, paper-specific comparison with no other possible source for the number: Table 1 and Table 11 (MHA-Abs/RoPE/xPos, H3, Hyena at custom non-public parameter counts, on a synthetic task the paper itself defines), Figure 8's inference-throughput bars and Table 15's memory benchmark (Appendix E.5: 'We measure the inference throughput of a Mamba... model... against a standard Transformer... We use the standard Transformer implementation in the Huggingface transformers library'; similarly 'We report measurements of the training memory requirements of 125M models... We compare to the most memory-efficient Transformer implementation'), and Table 13's HyenaDNA row (the paper modifies the classification task itself -- 'We modify the task to be significantly more challenging by classifying between the five great apes species' -- so HyenaDNA's numbers on this exact modified task could only have been produced by the Mamba authors' own rerun). Table 11's checkmark cells (footnote: '✓ denotes perfect generalization accuracy') are counted as own-result cells at value 100.0; ✗ (out of memory) cells are excluded as no result was produced. Open-ended deltas/ranges without a point value (abstract's '>1M tokens', 'reducing FID... by more than half', '20-40× faster', '4-5× higher throughput', '3× to 4× fewer parameters', 'over a 1.0 perplexity improvement') are excluded per the range rule. Appendix D's analytical byte-accounting figures (12/20/32/16 bytes of activations per token) are excluded as implementation/complexity analysis rather than a measured experimental result.
